corpus_audit.qualification: the retained corpus did not contain R_ARM_SBREL32; this milestone is driven by a source-confirmed RWPI relocation gap and an executed generated acceptance fixture, not a frequency claim

sbrel32_contract.abi_formula: S+A-B(S), stored as a complete 32-bit data word with no overflow check
sbrel32_contract.explicit_policy: --firmbolt-arm-static-base=segment-start declares B(S) to be the referenced symbol's fixed non-executable input PT_LOAD start
sbrel32_contract.handler: BOLT now recognizes, sizes, encodes and extracts the complete R_ARM_SBREL32 word and reconstructs its implicit SHT_REL addend against the declared B(S)
sbrel32_contract.transformation: ordinary FOP shrinks sbrel32_worker from 34 to 32 live bytes while preserving 14 exact instruction origins and the fixed typed RAM relocation
sbrel32_contract.verification: reference and candidate both load the relocated data word, add r9, dereference the resulting address and write RAM words [42, 42, 42] under the Cortex-M3 FastDyn fixture

scope_limits: AAELF32 leaves B(S) platform-defined; the segment-start interpretation remains opt-in firmware metadata rather than an inferred universal rule
without the explicit static-base contract, FirmBOLT preserves the already-linked data word and relocation but does not claim that it can rebase or relocate the referenced object
the accepted R_ARM_SBREL32 record and its storage remain fixed in RAM; data reordering, cloning and static-base changes are outside this milestone
generic AArch32 JITLink source-object BREL remains unsupported until its graph API carries the static-base origin explicitly
the production matrix demonstrates no regression across the existing firmware corpus, not complete x86-backend parity
the milestone establishes relocation, final-link publication and architectural execution correctness, not a performance result

source.pinned_lld: lld/ELF/Arch/ARM.cpp already implements R_ARM_SBREL32 as RE_ARM_SBREL and writes the complete 32-bit value
source.pinned_llvm_mc: llvm/lib/Target/ARM/MCTargetDesc/ARMELFObjectWriter.cpp emits R_ARM_SBREL32 for the sbrel data expression
